strategy.summary: Reproduce NumPy f2py/capi_maps selectedrealkind accuracy failure (selectedrealkind(16/32) returning -1) on the buggy revision by building/running NumPy for a 32-bit ARMHF/AArch32 environment, then run the project’s own selected test set where the buggy behavior manifests; verify that the added/modified test fails on the buggy commit and passes on the fixed one.

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (commit 77437b1474f1), running the project test suite via `numpy.test()` causes the selectedrealkind accuracy test to fail because it asserts that selectedrealkind(16) == 10 and selectedrealkind(32) == 16, but instead obtains -1. On the fixed revision, the same `numpy.test()` run makes that test pass with selectedrealkind returning the expected kinds for 16 and 32.
strategy.numerical_probe: selectedrealkind(16) and selectedrealkind(32) through NumPy’s f2py capi kind mapping (numpy.f2py.capi_maps.c2capi_map).
risks: Platform/toolchain dependence: the observed failure is explicitly tied to 32-bit ARMHF/AArch32 (issue mentions 32-bit userspace on 64-bit kernel; also ARMHF denormal/FTZ behavior is called out). If you run on x86_64/aarch64 or another ABI, the failure may not reproduce or the relevant f2py test may not be exercised.

Build flags/SIMD: behavior may depend on how ARM NEON code paths are compiled (and on the exact compiler/flags enabling ARM SIMD implementations). If your toolchain differs, the buggy behavior may not exist or may manifest differently.

The evidence does not include the exact pytest node id for the selectedrealkind test; the provided test command runs the entire NumPy test suite (`numpy.test()`). If the suite selection differs by revision, you may need to ensure the f2py tests are included (e.g., f2py enabled).

Dependency versions are not pinned in the provided evidence (unbounded constraints). If your environment installs incompatible pytest/hypothesis versions, the test suite selection/collection could differ; however, the strategy avoids forcing pins because no documented constraints were provided.

oracle.reference_source: NUMERICAL CHARACTERISTICS: expected selectedrealkind(16) -> 10 and selectedrealkind(32) -> 16; observed buggy behavior -> -1 for both.
oracle.why: The failure described is a discrete mismatch in returned kind integers (-1 vs expected positive integers), so the test should assert exact equality.

fails_on_buggy.description: What the assertion sees on the buggy revision, and why that makes it fail
fails_on_buggy.value: In the buggy revision, the selectedrealkind mapping returns -1 for both inputs 16 and 32, so assertions expecting 10 (for 16) and 16 (for 32) fail exact equality checks.

passes_on_fixed.description: What the test does on the fixed revision
passes_on_fixed.value: In the fixed revision, the selectedrealkind mapping returns 10 for input 16 and 16 for input 32, so the same exact-equality assertions succeed.
